cta.title: Stop Losing Time to GME Scheduling
cta.description: Book a call to talk through your scheduling needs and learn how Scheduling Wizard works. Join 30+ departments across 20+ hospitals and practices that have us build their call, block, clinic and shift schedules.

faq.answer: Most GME scheduling software is a self-service tool that requires chief residents to learn and operate a complex platform. Scheduling Wizard is different; it is a fully managed service. Programs submit their rules and receive finished, ACGME-compliant schedules as Excel files, with no software to learn or operate. The optimization is handled entirely by Scheduling Wizard's schedulers.
faq.question: What is GME scheduling software and how does Scheduling Wizard differ?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard builds in the ACGME duty hour regulations at schedule generation time. This means the 80-hour weekly limit, minimum rest requirements, and the 24-hour shift cap are built into the schedule itself, not checked manually after the fact. Subspecialty-specific ACGME rules are also built in, so programs do not need to cross-reference requirements themselves.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard ensure ACGME duty hour compliance?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard generates Block rotation schedules, Call schedules, Clinic schedules, and Attending schedules. All four schedule types are built together, so changes in one schedule type automatically propagate across the others and do not create downstream conflicts.
faq.question: What types of schedules does Scheduling Wizard generate for GME programs?

faq.answer: Yes. Scheduling Wizard handles schedule creation and optimization, while many clients continue using the platform they already have for day-to-day schedule access. Finished schedules are delivered as Excel files that can be uploaded directly into whichever platform your program already uses. There is no need to switch away from the platform you use now.
faq.question: Can Scheduling Wizard work alongside your existing platform?

faq.answer: Resident preferences including vacation requests, elective preferences, conference dates, moonlighting restrictions, and personal rules are submitted as inputs and factored into the optimization as first-class requirements. They are not manually patched in after the schedule is built, which means the final schedule reflects real program needs from the start.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard handle resident preferences and rules?

faq.answer: With Scheduling Wizard, institutional scheduling knowledge does not leave when a chief resident rotates out. Your program's rules, requests, and configurations are retained within the service year over year. Incoming chiefs inherit an optimized, working system rather than having to rebuild scheduling knowledge from scratch each academic year.
faq.question: What happens to scheduling knowledge when a new chief resident takes over?
